# Mzu 3D Solar System — factual product guide

## What it is

Mzu 3D Solar System is a free WebGL experience built with Three.js. Visitors can rotate and zoom the scene, click celestial objects, focus on individual planets, and follow a short guided tour. The site is designed for casual learning, visual exploration, classroom demonstrations, and space-themed embeds.

## What it is not

The scene is not a real-time model of the current Solar System. It does not calculate positions for a selected date and must not be used for observation planning or scientific research. Visual radii, orbit distances, and animation rates are deliberately compressed. Some textures and surface treatments are artistic or procedural.

## Interaction

- Drag to orbit the camera.
- Scroll or pinch to zoom.
- Select an object to reveal its available data and track it with the camera.
- Use the planet tour for a short introduction to the eight major planets.
- Use Share view to copy or send the current focus URL.
- Use Save image to download the rendered canvas as a PNG.
- Use Copy embed to copy a responsive iframe snippet. `?embed=1` hides the main interface for embedding.

## Data shown

Selectable objects may expose their name, type, visual radius, radius in kilometres, semi-major axis in astronomical units, visual orbit distance, and eccentricity. These values are reference fields; their on-screen rendering is not to scale.

## Technical notes

- Runs in modern browsers with WebGL.
- Uses a reduced-detail profile on smaller or lower-capability devices.
- No account or installation is required.
- Background music is optional and starts only after user action.
